From Tokyo to Hong Kong: Fast-fashion giant Shein says it plans to raise up to HK13.86bn (£1.3bn; $1.77bn) when its shares start trading on the Hong Kong stock market on 1 September.

In a filing on Monday, external, Shein said it will offer nearly 280 million shares for between HK$47.60 and HK$49.50.

At the top of the range, it would value the firm at almost $27bn (£19.8bn).

But that is much lower than the $100bn valuation it reached in a round of private fundraising in 2022, reflecting weaker sales growth and higher costs.

The company said it lost $99m in the first three months of the year, compared with a net income of $395m a year earlier.

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cdeweewjdxno?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss
source_title: Shein aims for almost $27bn valuation in stock market debut
source_summary: The fast-fashion giant's shares are due to start trading on the Hong Kong stock market on 1 September.

Scoreboard update: An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics.

Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.
